findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review. Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.fix: Separate the section by audience or clearly label each instruction with its intended reader (e.g., 'For employees:' or 'Manager sign-off:'), so each audience can identify which steps apply to them.
findings.violation: The section addresses at least three distinct audiences - employees, managers, and finance/payroll staff - in the same section with no separation or signal indicating which instructions apply to which reader, making it unclear who performs which actions.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Remove or relocate sentences that do not belong to the stipend policy's core message. Keep only: 'The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.' If the audit, federal guidance, and budget information are needed, place them in a separate 'Background' or 'Related Information' section with a clear label explaining their relevance.
findings.violation: The section presents four unrelated topics with no unifying theme: stipend coordination, a travel audit, federal remote-work guidance, and office administration. A reader cannot state what this section is about because it lacks a coherent thread connecting its sentences.

findings.evidence: The document uses 'stipend request' (line 17), 'final request' (line 23), 'employee request' (line 53), 'incomplete request' (line 29); and 'stipend item' (line 31), 'reimbursable item' (line 51), 'covered purchase amount' (line 52), and 'equipment' (line 45, 51) sometimes synonymously, sometimes for distinct process steps.
findings.fix: Choose one term for the request itself (e.g., always 'request' or always 'stipend request') and one term for reimbursable items (e.g., always 'equipment' or always 'covered item'), and use them consistently throughout. Add a glossary if terms must vary for technical reasons.
findings.location: Throughout the document, especially sections 'How to Apply', 'Required Documentation', 'Request Steps', and 'Terminology Notes'
findings.violation: Multiple terms refer to the same or nearly identical concepts without a signal that they are synonymous, forcing the reader to verify whether different terms name the same thing or different steps.

findings.evidence: After completing the main procedural sections (Eligibility through Restrictions), the document introduces 'Request Steps' with only one vague sentence: 'Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.' This is followed by sections on administrative processes and maintenance tasks that blur the boundary between employee-facing instructions and internal operations.
findings.fix: Either consolidate 'Request Steps' into 'How to Apply' with clear step-by-step formatting, or remove it entirely. Move administrative sections ('Program Coordination', 'Review Responsibility', 'Questions and Updates') to a separate 'For Administrators' section or footer so readers encounter only reader-facing content in the main body.
findings.location: Sections 8-13: 'Request Steps', 'Special Cases', 'Program Coordination', 'Review Responsibility', 'Questions and Updates'
findings.violation: Later sections lack clear purpose and organizational logic relative to the reader's task sequence. 'Request Steps' restates/clarifies material from 'How to Apply' without clear value, and administrative sections mix with reader-facing content.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing.
findings.fix: Move the interrupting clause elsewhere, or split it into its own sentence.
findings.violation: 3 comma-set-off clause(s) totalling 14 words intervene between the sentence's apparent subject and its verb.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The...
findings.fix: Open the paragraph with a transition word that states its relationship to the prior paragraph.
findings.violation: The paragraph opens with none of the fixed transition words, so the reader is not told how it relates to the paragraph before it.

findings.evidence: Examples: 'The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it' (line 7); 'The stipend clock resumes on their first day back' (line 13); 'the stipend request... moves to final processing' (line 21); 'An incomplete request pauses the timeline' (line 29); 'the policy applies to one device per category per employee' (line 47).
findings.fix: Replace abstract subjects with real actors: 'We supersede the prior version...' or 'Finance uses the current version...'; 'Your eligibility clock resumes...'; 'The benefits team moves your request...' or 'Your request moves to final processing when...'; 'Finance pauses the timeline...'; 'We apply the policy to one device...'
findings.violation: Multiple sentences use abstract nouns as subjects instead of naming the real-world actors responsible for the actions, requiring the reader to infer who actually performs each step.
